title: Multidimensional insights into the repeated electromagnetic field stimulation and biosystems interaction in aging and age-related diseases.
authors: Perez, Felipe P; Bandeira, Joseph P; Perez Chumbiauca, Cristina N; Lahiri, Debomoy K; Morisaki, Jorge; Rizkalla, Maher
one_liner_zh: 该文提出电磁场刺激通过RNA质子化激活HSF1进而与DNA结合调控衰老相关疾病的假说，涉及蛋白-DNA互作但缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，且非TF-DNA结合机制建模核心。
abstract: We provide a multidimensional sequence of events that describe the electromagnetic field (EMF) stimulation and biological system interaction. We describe this process from the quantum to the molecular, cellular, and organismal levels. We hypothesized that the sequence of events of these interactions starts with the oscillatory effect of the repeated electromagnetic stimulation (REMFS). These oscillations affect the interfacial water of an RNA causing changes at the quantum and molecular levels that release protons by quantum tunneling. Then protonation of RNA produces conformational changes that allow it to bind and activate Heat Shock Transcription Factor 1 (HSF1). Activated HSF1 binds to the DNA expressing chaperones that help regulate autophagy and degradation of abnormal proteins. This action helps to prevent and treat diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease (PD) by increasing clearance of pathologic proteins. This framework is based on multiple mathematical models, computer simulations, biophysical experiments, and cellular and animal studies. Results of the literature review and our research point towards the capacity of REMFS to manipulate various networks altered in aging (Reale et al. PloS one 9, e104973, 2014), including delay of cellular senescence (Perez et al. 2008, Exp Gerontol 43, 307-316) and reduction in levels of amyloid-beta peptides (Abeta) (Perez et al. 2021, Sci Rep 11, 621). Results of these experiments using REMFS at low frequencies can be applied to the treatment of patients with age-related diseases. The use of EMF as a non-invasive therapeutic modality for Alzheimer's disease, specifically, holds promise. It is also necessary to consider the complicated and interconnected genetic and epigenetic effects of the REMFS-biological system's interaction while avoiding any possible adverse effects.
abstract_zh: 我们提供了一组多维事件序列，用以描述电磁场（EMF）刺激与生物系统之间的相互作用。我们从量子层面到分子、细胞及生物体层面描述了这一过程。我们假设这些相互作用的序列事件始于重复电磁刺激（REMFS）的振荡效应。这些振荡影响RNA的界面水，导致量子和分子层面的变化，通过量子隧穿释放质子。随后，RNA的质子化引发构象变化，使其能够结合并激活热休克转录因子1（HSF1）。激活的HSF1结合DNA，表达伴侣蛋白，这些伴侣蛋白有助于调节自噬和异常蛋白质的降解。这一作用通过增加病理性蛋白质的清除，有助于预防和治疗阿尔茨海默病和帕金森病（PD）等疾病。该框架基于多种数学模型、计算机模拟、生物物理实验以及细胞和动物研究。文献回顾和我们的研究结果表明，REMFS能够操纵衰老过程中改变的各种网络（Reale等人，PloS one 9, e104973, 2014），包括延缓细胞衰老（Perez等人，2008, Exp Gerontol 43, 307-316）以及降低淀粉样β肽（Abeta）水平（Perez等人，2021, Sci Rep 11, 621）。使用低频REMFS进行的这些实验结果可应用于年龄相关疾病患者的治疗。特别是，将EMF作为阿尔茨海默病的非侵入性治疗手段具有前景。同时，还需考虑REMFS-生物系统相互作用中复杂且相互关联的遗传和表观遗传效应，并避免任何潜在的不良影响。
